task_3.title: Warn on unsupported revision requests for local-recipes-index remotes
task_3.description: The upgrade adds clearer feedback when a consumer requests a recipe revision from a local-recipes-index remote that does not match the currently available source revision. Instead of only failing resolution, the client now warns that the remote cannot serve arbitrary specific revisions and then preserves the not-found failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that requesting a specific recipe revision from a `local-recipes-index` remote produces a clear warning when the requested revision is different from the currently available revision, while still failing resolution for that unavailable revision.

expectation.grounded: When `local-recipes-index` resolution reaches `get_recipe_revision_reference(ref)` and the exported reference differs from the requested `ref`, the client should emit a warning through the user-facing output indicating that the requested specific revision does not match the current source revision and that `local-recipes-index` cannot provide a specific revision, then raise `RecipeNotFoundException(ref)`. If the exported reference matches the request, the method should continue returning the resolved reference.
expectation.conceptual: If a user asks a local-recipes-index remote for a recipe revision that is not the one currently available in that source, the client should explain that the remote cannot serve that exact revision and should still report the revision as unavailable. Requests that already match the currently available revision should continue to resolve normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful resolution when the requested recipe reference already matches the current exported revision. Do not suppress the existing `RecipeNotFoundException` failure for unavailable specific revisions. Limit the added warning behavior to the mismatched specific-revision case for `local-recipes-index` remotes.
constraints.conceptual: Normal installs must keep working as before, and unsupported revision requests must still fail. The only new observable behavior should be clearer guidance in the case where a local index remote cannot honor an explicitly requested different revision.

behavior: A request for a specific recipe revision against a `local-recipes-index` remote now emits a warning before failing when the requested revision differs from the revision currently available in the source.
The failure mode remains a recipe-not-found outcome for that requested revision.
If the requested recipe reference matches the currently available revision, the reference continues to resolve without the new warning.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer requests a recipe with an explicit revision from a `local-recipes-index` remote and that revision is not the current available revision, the client should show a warning explaining that the remote cannot provide that specific revision.
When the same mismatched revision request is processed, the operation should still fail as a recipe-not-found condition for the requested reference.
When a requested recipe revision on a `local-recipes-index` remote matches the current available revision, the operation should complete with normal resolution behavior and no mismatch warning.

task_1.title: Expose FOUND and VERSION for additional CMake Find prefixes
task_1.description: Conan 2.13.0 updates CMakeDeps-generated Find modules so any extra variable prefixes configured for a dependency also expose standard package discovery state and version variables. This lets CMake consumers using alternate or legacy prefixes observe package availability and version consistently in generated Find modules.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeDeps-generated Find modules expose consistent package discovery variables for every prefix declared through `cmake_additional_variables_prefixes`, so consumers using alternate or legacy prefixes can detect whether the package was found and read its version.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeDeps` generates a `Find<name>.cmake` module for a dependency that declares `cmake_additional_variables_prefixes`, the generated module should define `{prefix}_FOUND` and `{prefix}_VERSION` for each configured prefix in addition to the existing primary package discovery variables. `{prefix}_FOUND` should indicate a successful find result for that module, and `{prefix}_VERSION` should expose the dependency version under the same additional prefix.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake Find modules should treat configured alternate prefixes as first-class aliases for package discovery. Consumers checking an alternate prefix should be able to tell that the package was found and know which version was resolved, just as they can with the main package prefix.

constraints.grounded: This applies only to `Find*.cmake` output generated by `CMakeDeps` and only for prefixes explicitly listed in `cmake_additional_variables_prefixes`. Existing primary `*_FOUND` and `*_VERSION` variables for the generated package name must remain available and unchanged for consumers already depending on them.
constraints.conceptual: Do not alter discovery behavior for packages that do not opt into extra prefixes, and do not remove or rename the existing default discovery variables.

behavior: Generated `Find*.cmake` modules now define `<prefix>_FOUND` for every configured additional variables prefix.
Each generated `<prefix>_FOUND` reports the package as found when the enclosing Find module resolves successfully.
Generated `Find*.cmake` modules now define `<prefix>_VERSION` for every configured additional variables prefix.
Each generated `<prefix>_VERSION` exposes the resolved dependency version under the same alternate prefix.
The main package discovery variables remain present; the additional prefixed variables are added alongside the existing ones rather than replacing them.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dependency that configures one or more `cmake_additional_variables_prefixes`, when `CMakeDeps` generates a `Find*.cmake` module for that dependency, the module should expose `<prefix>_FOUND` for each configured prefix.
Given the same generated `Find*.cmake` module, when a consumer reads `<prefix>_VERSION`, it should receive the dependency version for each configured prefix.
When a consumer continues using the main generated package prefix, its existing `*_FOUND` and `*_VERSION` variables should still be available.
When no `cmake_additional_variables_prefixes` are configured, generated `Find*.cmake` behavior should remain unchanged aside from not having extra prefixed discovery variables.

task_2.title: Expose incubating CMakeConfigDeps generator
task_2.description: Conan 2.13.0 adds a new incubating `CMakeConfigDeps` generator as an explicit opt-in alternative for CMake dependency configuration. The generator is now available as a public Conan generator entry point, but it must remain behind the `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new` configuration gate, emit an experimental warning when enabled, and fail fast when referenced without that gate. Existing `CMakeDeps` usage stays stable unless the stronger opt-in value is selected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.13.0 exposes the new incubating `CMakeConfigDeps` generator for Conan users while keeping it explicitly gated, warning that it is experimental when enabled, and preventing it from being used silently without the required `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new` opt-in.

expectation.grounded: Conan 2.13.0 must accept `CMakeConfigDeps` as a public generator entry point from `conan.tools.cmake` and from generator declarations. Using `CMakeConfigDeps` must require `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new` to be set to an allowed incubating value such as `will_break_next` or `recipe_will_break`; when enabled it should instantiate the new CMake config-deps implementation and emit a warning that the feature is incubating. If `CMakeConfigDeps` is referenced without that conf enabled, Conan must raise `ConanException` instead of falling back to legacy behavior. Existing `CMakeDeps` behavior must continue to switch to the new implementation only when the conf value is `will_break_next`, while still recognizing `recipe_will_break` as a valid gate value.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to opt into a new experimental CMake dependency configuration generator during Conan installs and generation flows. The feature must be clearly marked as experimental, require an explicit configuration opt-in, and fail clearly if referenced without that opt-in. Existing stable `CMakeDeps` behavior should remain unchanged unless users explicitly request the new behavior.

constraints.grounded: `CMakeConfigDeps` must remain disabled by default and must not silently behave like legacy `CMakeDeps` when the conf gate is absent. The generator name and helper API must both honor the same incubating gate. Accepting `recipe_will_break` as a valid conf choice must not cause plain `CMakeDeps` to switch to the new implementation unless the value is specifically `will_break_next`.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve backward compatibility for existing CMake dependency generation by default, keep the new generator strictly opt-in, and avoid implicit fallback or surprise activation when the experimental gate is missing or only partially enabled.

behavior: `CMakeConfigDeps` is added as a public CMake generator entry point and can be referenced directly by Conan generator declarations.
When `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new` is enabled with an incubating value, `CMakeConfigDeps` resolves to the new implementation and emits an experimental-feature warning.
When `CMakeConfigDeps` is used without enabling `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new`, Conan raises `ConanException` instead of proceeding with legacy dependency generation.

`CMakeDeps` now accepts both incubating conf values, but only `will_break_next` switches `CMakeDeps` itself to the new implementation; `recipe_will_break` leaves standard `CMakeDeps` behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan recipe imports or declares `CMakeConfigDeps` and `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new` is enabled with an allowed incubating value, Conan should recognize the generator, create the new config-deps generator, and warn that it is experimental.

When a Conan recipe, generator attribute, or generator declaration references `CMakeConfigDeps` without enabling `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new`, Conan should stop with `ConanException` rather than silently generating output with legacy `CMakeDeps` behavior.

When users continue to use `CMakeDeps`, setting `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new=will_break_next` should activate the new implementation, while `tools.cmake.cmakedeps:new=recipe_will_break` should remain a recognized gate value without changing standard `CMakeDeps` behavior.
When the experimental gate is not set, existing `CMakeDeps` workflows should continue to behave as before and should not be affected by the presence of the new `CMakeConfigDeps` API.

task_4.title: Expose repository selection in coordinates_to_conandata
task_4.description: The Git SCM helper now lets callers choose whether coordinates captured into conandata should use the repository-level selection supported by get_url_and_commit(), while keeping the previous default behavior unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Git SCM coordinate capture can opt into repository-level resolution when saving source coordinates to conandata, without changing the existing default behavior for current callers.

expectation.grounded: The public API Git.coordinates_to_conandata() should accept an optional repository parameter with the same default used by Git.get_url_and_commit(). When invoked, it should obtain SCM coordinates through Git.get_url_and_commit(repository=...) and persist the returned URL and commit under the scm entry in conandata.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to request repository-level SCM coordinates when exporting Git metadata to conandata, while calls that do not opt in should continue to behave as before.

constraints.grounded: Calling Git.coordinates_to_conandata() with no arguments must preserve the prior default selection semantics. The new parameter must align with the repository behavior already exposed by Git.get_url_and_commit(), including the distinction between the defined folder selection and repository-level selection.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must add capability without breaking existing recipes: current calls keep their existing result, and opting in only changes which SCM coordinates are captured.

behavior: Git.coordinates_to_conandata() accepts an optional repository argument.
When repository is not provided, Git.coordinates_to_conandata() uses the same default SCM coordinate resolution as before.
When repository is provided, Git.coordinates_to_conandata() forwards that setting to Git.get_url_and_commit().
The URL and commit returned by Git.get_url_and_commit(repository=...) are stored in conandata under the scm key.
Using repository=true enables repository-level coordinate capture instead of the defined-folder commit selection.
acceptance_criteria: When Git.coordinates_to_conandata() is called without arguments, it should persist scm URL and commit values using the same default behavior as in the previous version.
When Git.coordinates_to_conandata(repository=false) is called, it should persist SCM coordinates using the defined-folder selection supported by Git.get_url_and_commit().
When Git.coordinates_to_conandata(repository=true) is called, it should persist SCM coordinates using the repository-level selection supported by Git.get_url_and_commit().
When SCM coordinates are captured through Git.coordinates_to_conandata(), the persisted conandata entry should still contain scm.url and scm.commit values.

task_5.title: Support MCF threading in GCC MinGW settings
task_5.description: The update adds support for the `mcf` threading model to the built-in GCC MinGW compiler settings so newer MinGW toolchains can be configured without custom settings overrides.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that GCC MinGW configurations can declare the `mcf` threading model as a supported compiler setting so newer `mingw-builds` toolchains work out of the box.

expectation.grounded: The built-in GCC Windows MinGW `compiler.threads` setting must accept `mcf` as a valid value in addition to the previously supported values. User profiles, dependency settings, and package configurations that specify `compiler.threads=mcf` for GCC MinGW must be treated as valid configuration input instead of being rejected as an unsupported setting value.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select the MCF threading model for MinGW GCC in normal configuration flows, and projects using that toolchain should no longer require manual settings customization just to recognize that threading option.

constraints.grounded: Existing GCC MinGW `compiler.threads` values remain supported unchanged, and this update only expands the accepted value set for that public setting; it does not imply new behavior for other compiler settings or other compiler families.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be additive only: current MinGW GCC configurations must keep working as before, while the new threading option becomes available without altering unrelated compiler behavior.

behavior: The recognized GCC MinGW `compiler.threads` values now include `mcf`.
Configurations that declare `compiler.threads=mcf` for GCC on Windows MinGW are accepted by the built-in settings model.
Newer `mingw-builds` toolchains that use the MCF threading model can be represented with default settings, avoiding the need for user-supplied settings extensions.
Previously supported GCC MinGW threading values continue to be accepted with no behavioral change.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures GCC for Windows MinGW with `compiler.threads=mcf`, the configuration should be accepted as a valid built-in setting.
When a project or package depends on a MinGW GCC toolchain that uses the MCF threading model, it should be configurable without requiring a custom settings definition for that threading value.
When existing GCC MinGW configurations use previously supported threading values, they should continue to behave as before.
When using compiler families or settings outside the GCC MinGW threading setting, the update should not change their accepted values or observable behavior.

task_7.title: Add incubating monolithic workspace install flow
task_7.description: Conan 2.13.0 adds an incubating `workspace install` command for multi-editable workspaces so external dependencies can be resolved and generator output can be produced once for the workspace as a monolithic consumer, while keeping editable packages collapsed out of the generated dependency outputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that workspaces with multiple editable packages can be installed as a single monolithic consumer using `conan workspace install`, so users can generate one shared install result for the workspace while only external dependencies are installed and surfaced as consumer dependencies.

expectation.grounded: When the incubating workspace feature is enabled, `conan workspace install` should accept standard install arguments such as generators, output folder, lockfile, profiles, remotes, build/update modes, and install the current workspace as one consumer. The command should require at least one editable package in the workspace, load a graph from those editable references, collapse editable-to-editable relationships out of the final consumer graph, analyze and install binaries for non-editable dependencies, and generate a single install result for the workspace root. If the workspace provides a custom root consumer definition, that root should be used; otherwise the install should fall back to a default virtual consumer.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to install an entire workspace once, rather than installing each editable package separately. The install result should represent the workspace as one top-level consumer, include only external dependencies in generated consumer outputs, and honor normal install options and profile/lockfile resolution.

constraints.grounded: The `workspace` command surface remains gated behind the incubating feature enablement flag. `workspace install` must fail for workspaces with no editables. A custom workspace root consumer may shape the root install context, but it must not declare its own package requirements or recipe lifecycle methods that would make it behave like a normal package recipe. `workspace build` should still reject attempts to build all products when the workspace defines no products.
constraints.conceptual: This feature is opt-in and intentionally limited. It only applies to enabled workspaces, it only works when the workspace actually contains editable packages, and custom workspace-level configuration can customize the root consumer context without redefining dependency ownership or package build logic.

behavior: `conan workspace install` is available as a new workspace subcommand for monolithic installation of a workspace.
The command resolves the workspace's editable package references, builds a dependency graph from them, and treats the workspace root as the single consumer install target.
Editable packages inside the workspace are collapsed out of the final consumer dependency graph so generated consumer outputs reflect only external dependencies.
The install flow analyzes and installs binaries for the collapsed graph and emits one shared generator/output set for the workspace root, optionally under a user-selected output folder.
If the workspace defines a custom root consumer, that definition is used as the workspace install root; otherwise installation proceeds with a default virtual consumer root.
Workspace installation fails when no editable packages are present in the workspace.
Workspace commands are blocked unless the incubating workspace feature is explicitly enabled.
acceptance_criteria: When an enabled workspace contains one or more editable packages and the user runs `conan workspace install`, it should complete a single install flow for the workspace root rather than requiring separate installs per editable package.

When `conan workspace install` completes, the generated consumer outputs should include external dependencies needed by the workspace and should not expose editable workspace packages as installed external package dependencies.

When the user passes normal install-time options such as profiles, lockfiles, remotes, generators, build/update settings, or an output folder, `conan workspace install` should honor them consistently with an install operation on a consumer.
When the workspace has no editable packages, `conan workspace install` should fail instead of producing install artifacts.

When a custom workspace root consumer is provided, installation should use it only as the root consumer context and reject configurations that add their own package dependency declarations or package recipe lifecycle behavior.
When the incubating workspace feature is not enabled, invoking workspace commands should fail instead of silently running.

task_6.title: Migrate Conan workspaces to the new class-based `conanws.py` model
task_6.description: Conan 2.13.0 replaces the ad hoc `conanws.py` module contract with a public `Workspace` base class, aligning workspace definitions with `ConanFile`. Custom workspaces now read YAML data through `conan_data`, use built-in workspace helpers instead of injected collaborators, and can participate in a workspace-level install flow that collapses editables into a single root for installing external dependencies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that custom Conan workspaces are defined with the new class-based `conanws.py` contract so workspace metadata, editable package discovery, and workspace-level installs behave consistently with Conan 2.13.0.

expectation.grounded: `conanws.py` should define exactly one subclass of `conan.Workspace`, and Conan should instantiate that class when loading a workspace. The workspace instance should expose YAML-backed data through `self.conan_data`, workspace location through `self.folder`, scoped output through `self.output`, and helper loading through `load_conanfile()`. Overrides of public workspace behaviors such as `name()`, `home_folder()`, `editables()`, `products()`, `add()`, `remove()`, and `root_conanfile()` should be honored. `conan workspace install` should collapse all workspace editables into one root install context, install only external dependencies, and generate a single install result for the workspace.
expectation.conceptual: Workspace customization should follow the same object-oriented pattern as package recipes: a workspace file defines one workspace class, can read shared YAML configuration, can customize how editables and metadata are derived, and can install the whole workspace as one consumer-facing unit instead of handling each editable independently.

constraints.grounded: YAML-only workspaces must continue to work when `conanws.py` is absent. If `conanws.py` is present, loading must fail when it does not define exactly one `Workspace` subclass. Editable paths and optional output folders must resolve inside the workspace, and resolved editable entries must point to existing `conanfile.py` files. `conan workspace install` must fail when the workspace has no editables. If `root_conanfile()` is provided for workspace install, the returned root class cannot declare its own requirements or recipe build/source/package methods. Workspace commands remain gated by `CONAN_WORKSPACE_ENABLE`.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve simple YAML-based workspaces, reject ambiguous or invalid custom workspace definitions early, keep editable references bounded to the workspace itself, and avoid treating a workspace install as a collection of separate editable installs. Any custom root used for whole-workspace installation should only describe the workspace shell, not redefine package behavior.

behavior: A discovered workspace is now loaded from `conanws.py` by instantiating a single `Workspace` subclass; module-level workspace attributes and functions are no longer the active customization model.
Workspace YAML data from `conanws.yml` is exposed as `self.conan_data`, removing the need for injected `conanws_data` state and enabling the workspace class to read configuration directly.

The public `Workspace` base class provides built-in helpers and state, including workspace-relative editable persistence, workspace-scoped output, and `load_conanfile()` for loading editables from workspace-relative package folders.

Workspace editable definitions are normalized into absolute `conanfile.py` locations for runtime use, and Conan raises an error if an editable path is missing, not absolute when persisted, or escapes the workspace boundary.

Workspace add/remove operations now dispatch through the workspace instance, so custom `Workspace` subclasses can override those operations while still using the default YAML-backed persistence behavior.

A new `conan workspace install` flow installs the workspace as a monolith: it requires at least one editable, collapses editable nodes into a single root context, installs only non-editable external dependencies, and generates one install result for the workspace.

If a workspace provides `root_conanfile()` for the collapsed install root, Conan uses it only as a lightweight root descriptor and rejects recipe-style requirement/build/source/package declarations on that root.
Workspace command usage and automatic workspace activation remain disabled unless the incubating feature gate is explicitly enabled.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace folder contains only `conanws.yml`, Conan should still discover the workspace and use the default YAML-backed workspace behavior.

When `conanws.py` defines one subclass of `conan.Workspace`, Conan should load that class, expose YAML configuration through `self.conan_data`, and honor overridden workspace methods such as naming, home folder resolution, editable discovery, and add/remove behavior.

When `conanws.py` defines no `Workspace` subclass or defines more than one, workspace loading should fail with a workspace definition error instead of falling back to module-level attributes or injected helpers.
When a workspace reports editable entries, Conan should resolve them to actual `conanfile.py` files under the workspace root and reject missing or out-of-workspace editable paths.

When `conan workspace install` runs against a workspace with editables, it should install only external dependencies and produce a single workspace-level install result rather than treating each editable as an independent consumer install.
When `conan workspace install` runs against a workspace with no editables, it should fail rather than performing a no-op install.

When a custom root is supplied through `root_conanfile()` for workspace installation, Conan should accept it only if it acts as a lightweight workspace root and does not declare recipe requirements or build/source/package behaviors.
When the workspace incubating feature gate is not enabled, workspace commands should remain unavailable even if a workspace definition is present.

task_8.title: Generate an install-ready CMake workspace scaffold
task_8.description: The built-in `conan new workspace` template now creates a monolithic CMake super-project and workspace root configuration that are ready to work with `conan workspace install`, while preserving the default editable package layout and dependency chain.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan new workspace` generates a default workspace that users can open and use as a monolithic CMake super-project with `conan workspace install`, without losing the standard editable products or their dependency relationships.

expectation.grounded: Running the built-in `workspace` template should generate `conanws.yml`, a root `CMakeLists.txt`, a workspace root `conanws.py`, a `.gitignore` for the build folder, and the editable projects `liba`, `libb`, and `app1`. The generated `conanws.py` should provide a workspace root `ConanFile` configured for `cmake_layout`, `CMakeDeps`, and `CMakeToolchain`, exposed through `Workspace.root_conanfile()`, so the scaffold is compatible with `conan workspace install`. The editable dependency chain should remain `libb -> liba/0.1` and `app1 -> libb/0.1`, and built-in workspace-template rendering should preserve the primary editable package name as `liba` even when additional template definitions are supplied.
expectation.conceptual: Creating a new workspace should produce a ready-to-use multi-project CMake starter that supports Conan workspace installation flows out of the box. Users should receive a complete top-level workspace build setup, and optional template inputs should extend the starter package behavior without changing the default workspace topology or package identities.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the visible editable products created by the default workspace template or their package references; `liba/0.1`, `libb/0.1`, and `app1/0.1` must remain the generated workspace members. The special handling for preserving `liba` as the default primary package name must apply only to the built-in `workspace` template and must not alter template rendering behavior for unrelated templates. The generated workspace root definition is for layout and generator configuration, not for introducing separate workspace-level package requirements.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the default starter workspace recognizable and backward-compatible for users of the built-in workspace template. The new install-ready behavior must add top-level workspace support without renaming the generated packages, changing their default relationships, or affecting other templates.

behavior: `conan new workspace` now creates a top-level CMake super-project in addition to the workspace manifest and sample editable projects.
The generated workspace includes a root Conan workspace configuration file so `conan workspace install` has explicit workspace-level layout and generator settings.
The scaffolded super-project aggregates `liba`, `libb`, and `app1` as local CMake subprojects intended to participate in a monolithic build.
The default editable dependency flow remains `liba` as the base library, `libb` depending on `liba/0.1`, and `app1` depending on `libb/0.1`.

When users pass additional definitions to the built-in workspace template, those definitions can still affect the primary editable content, but they must not replace the primary editable's default package identity of `liba`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan new workspace`, the generated workspace should include root-level files for workspace metadata, monolithic CMake configuration, workspace Conan configuration, and build-folder ignore rules, along with the sample projects `liba`, `libb`, and `app1`.
When the generated workspace is examined through normal workspace commands, it should expose the editable products `liba/0.1`, `libb/0.1`, and `app1/0.1`.

When a user runs `conan workspace install` in the generated workspace, the scaffold should already contain the required workspace-level Conan and CMake entrypoints needed for a monolithic CMake install flow.

When a user creates the built-in workspace template with extra template definitions such as additional requirements, the generated primary library should still identify as `liba` and the default `libb` and `app1` dependency chain should remain intact.

task_9.title: New CMakeDeps adds library and include search paths
task_9.description: The 2.13.0 update expands the new CMakeDeps path generation so CMake consumers automatically receive dependency library and header search paths in addition to executable lookup paths. This reduces manual CMake path setup and defines how host, test, and build dependency contexts contribute when multiple packages expose overlapping search locations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using the new CMakeDeps generator automatically expose dependency library, header, and tool search locations to CMake so consumers can resolve packages without manually extending search paths.

expectation.grounded: When the new CMakeDeps generator is used, the generated CMake path configuration should prepend dependency bindirs to CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH, dependency libdirs to CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH, and dependency includedirs to CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH when those directories are declared in Conan package metadata. CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH should keep using only direct dependencies from host, test, and direct build contexts, while CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH and CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH should use host and test requirements, including transitive ones. If the same package name contributes more than once to the same CMake path variable from different contexts, Conan should keep a single contribution for that package name and emit an informational notice identifying that a context-specific choice was made.
expectation.conceptual: Using the new CMakeDeps flow should make CMake aware of dependency executables, libraries, and headers automatically. Tool lookup should remain limited to directly declared dependencies, while library and header lookup should also work through applicable host and test dependency graphs, and overlapping contributions should resolve deterministically with a visible notice.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH support for direct dependencies. Only prepend a CMake path variable when contributing directories exist for that variable. Do not add library or include search paths from direct build requirements. Preserve deterministic de-duplication by package name for each CMake path variable and surface the conflict through Conan output instead of emitting multiple entries for the same package name contribution.
constraints.conceptual: Existing executable discovery behavior must continue to work, new search paths should appear only when dependencies actually expose them, build-only tools must not start affecting library or header lookup, and duplicate dependency contributions must resolve predictably rather than producing ambiguous search order.

behavior: The new CMakeDeps-generated path configuration now prepends CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH from dependency libdirs.
The new CMakeDeps-generated path configuration now prepends CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH from dependency includedirs.
CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH continues to be populated only from direct dependencies, across host, test, and direct build contexts.

CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH and CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH are populated from host and test requirements without restricting contributions to direct dependencies, so transitive host or test dependencies can contribute library and include directories.

If multiple contributing dependencies share the same package name for a given CMake path variable, the generator keeps one contribution for that package name and emits an informational notice that the selected contribution depends on dependency context.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer uses the new CMakeDeps generator and a host or test dependency declares library directories, the generated CMake configuration should prepend those directories to CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH.
When a consumer uses the new CMakeDeps generator and a host or test dependency declares include directories, the generated CMake configuration should prepend those directories to CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH.
When a transitive host or test dependency declares library or include directories, those directories should still be present in the generated CMake search paths.

When a direct dependency declares executable directories, those directories should continue to appear in CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH, including direct build requirements, while build requirements should not add entries to CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH or CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH.

When the same package name contributes to the same CMake path variable from multiple dependency contexts, the generated configuration should retain one effective contribution for that package name and Conan should report that a context-based selection occurred.

task_11.title: Expose dependency extension properties to Conan extensions
task_11.description: Conan 2.13.0 adds access to dependency-level extension properties from dependency objects exposed to recipes and extensions. This lets plugin logic inspect metadata declared by dependencies, including for custom transitive decisions, while safely treating dependencies without such metadata as empty.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan extensions and recipe-side dependency inspection can read `extension_properties` from dependency entries so dependency metadata can participate in user-visible behaviors such as custom compatibility or transitive policy decisions, without failing when a dependency does not define any extension properties.

expectation.grounded: Objects obtained from `conanfile.dependencies` must expose an `extension_properties` attribute. When the dependency recipe defines `extension_properties`, consumers should receive that mapping through the dependency object; when it does not, the dependency object should expose an empty mapping instead of raising an attribute error. This access is available for extensions/plugins that inspect dependencies and derive behavior from dependency metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to Conan 2.13.0 should be able to build extensions and dependency-aware logic that read extension metadata from dependencies directly. Dependency metadata should be observable consistently across the dependency graph, and missing metadata should behave as empty rather than causing failures.

constraints.grounded: Reading `extension_properties` from a dependency must be backward compatible for dependencies that never declared that attribute. The change should add dependency metadata visibility without changing unrelated dependency access patterns, and any transitive interpretation of that metadata remains the responsibility of the consuming extension or plugin.
constraints.conceptual: Existing consumers should not break when some dependencies do not provide extension metadata. The upgrade should expand what metadata can be observed from dependencies, but it should not automatically impose new transitive rules unless user logic explicitly does so.

behavior: Dependency objects exposed through `conanfile.dependencies` now provide an `extension_properties` attribute.
If a dependency recipe defines `extension_properties`, upstream consumers can inspect those values from the dependency object.
If a dependency recipe does not define `extension_properties`, accessing the attribute on the dependency object yields an empty mapping instead of failing.
Extensions and plugins can use dependency `extension_properties` to implement custom graph-wide or transitive behavior based on dependency metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When extension or recipe logic iterates over `conanfile.dependencies.values()`, each dependency should allow access to `extension_properties`.
When a dependency declares custom `extension_properties`, reading `dep.extension_properties` from an upstream consumer should expose those declared values.
When a dependency does not declare any `extension_properties`, reading `dep.extension_properties` should succeed and behave as an empty property set.

When users implement extension logic that depends on dependency metadata, the logic should be able to use dependency `extension_properties` directly rather than requiring out-of-band access to that metadata.

task_10.title: Expose library and include search paths in new CMakeDeps
task_10.description: The 2.13.0 update expands the new CMakeDeps path generation so CMake consumers receive dependency library and include search paths in addition to executable search paths. This makes host and test dependency headers and libraries discoverable through standard CMake path variables while keeping executable lookup rules scoped to direct dependencies and resolving duplicate package-name contributors deterministically.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using the new CMakeDeps generator automatically expose dependency library and include directories to CMake, while preserving existing executable path behavior and deterministic handling when the same package name contributes paths from multiple dependency contexts.

expectation.grounded: When the new CMakeDeps generator produces `conan_cmakedeps_paths.cmake`, it must prepend `CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH` from dependency `cpp_info.libdirs` and `CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH` from dependency `cpp_info.includedirs` for host and test requirements, including transitive ones. `CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH` must continue to be populated from `cpp_info.bindirs` of direct requirements only across host, test, and build contexts. If multiple requirements with the same package name contribute to one of these CMake path variables, generation should keep a single contributor for that package name and emit an informational notice indicating that the context-selected contribution is being used.
expectation.conceptual: Using the new CMakeDeps generator should make dependency headers and libraries discoverable by normal CMake search behavior without extra manual path setup. Executable lookup should remain limited to direct dependencies, and conflicting contributions from the same package name should resolve predictably with a visible notice.

constraints.grounded: Do not add build-requirement library or include directories to `CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH` or `CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH`. Do not broaden `CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH` to transitive dependencies. Existing package config path exports and runtime debugger environment behavior must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: The new search-path support must not leak tool-only header or library directories into consumer resolution, and it must not change existing executable discovery beyond the current direct-dependency scope.

behavior: The generated CMakeDeps path file now prepends `CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH` with library directories contributed by host and test dependencies.
The generated CMakeDeps path file now prepends `CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH` with include directories contributed by host and test dependencies.
Library and include path propagation applies to transitive host and test dependencies, not only direct ones.
Program path propagation remains based on `CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH` from direct dependencies only, including direct build requirements.

If more than one dependency with the same package name contributes to a given CMake path variable, Conan keeps one contribution for that package name and emits an informational notice about the selected context.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer uses the new CMakeDeps generator with a dependency that defines library directories, the generated CMake environment should expose those directories through `CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH` without requiring manual additions.

When a consumer uses the new CMakeDeps generator with a dependency that defines include directories, the generated CMake environment should expose those directories through `CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH` without requiring manual additions.
When a host or test dependency is brought in transitively, its include and library directories should still be available through the generated CMake path configuration.
When a dependency contributes only transitively, its binary directories should not become discoverable through `CMAKE_PROGRAM_PATH` unless that dependency is also a direct requirement.

When the same package name contributes to the same CMake path variable from multiple dependency contexts, generation should choose one contribution predictably and surface an informational notice that a context-specific value was used.

task_12.title: Add direct version-range checks on Version objects
task_12.description: Version 2.13.0 adds a user-facing convenience API that lets callers ask a Version instance whether it satisfies a version range string directly, while preserving the library's existing range parsing and prerelease-resolution behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that consumers can evaluate whether a `Version` instance matches a version range expression directly from the `Version` object, including control over prerelease resolution, without requiring a separate range object in user code.

expectation.grounded: Expose a new `Version.in_range(version_range, resolve_prerelease=None)` instance method. For a supplied range expression string, it should evaluate the current `Version` against the existing `VersionRange` matching rules and return a boolean result. The optional `resolve_prerelease` argument should be forwarded to range evaluation so prerelease inclusion follows the same policy controls already supported by version-range matching.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to call `in_range()` on a version object to check whether it falls within a declared version range. The result should match the library's existing interpretation of range expressions, and callers should be able to opt into or override prerelease handling when needed.

constraints.grounded: The new API should preserve the same acceptance and rejection semantics as `VersionRange` evaluation, including default behavior when `resolve_prerelease` is omitted and the same failure behavior for invalid range expressions. It should add a direct check on `Version` without changing version ordering semantics.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a convenience addition, not a semantic rewrite. Existing version comparison and range-matching behavior should stay consistent, and malformed range inputs should fail the same way they already do elsewhere in the library.

behavior: A `Version` instance now provides an `in_range()` method for evaluating membership in a version range expression.
Calling `in_range()` with a valid range string returns a boolean indicating whether that version satisfies the specified range.
The `resolve_prerelease` parameter is optional and influences range evaluation using the same prerelease-resolution rules already used by version-range matching.
If the supplied range expression cannot be interpreted by the existing range parser, `in_range()` surfaces the same error behavior as direct `VersionRange` usage.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller has a `Version` object and a valid version range expression, calling `in_range()` should return whether the version matches that range according to existing library rules.
When `resolve_prerelease` is provided, `in_range()` should honor that prerelease policy during range evaluation.
When `resolve_prerelease` is omitted, `in_range()` should use the library's default prerelease behavior for version-range checks.
When the range expression is invalid, calling `in_range()` should fail in the same way as evaluating the same expression through the existing version-range API.

task_15.title: Expand Premake wrapper configuration and action handling
task_15.description: The Premake integration now supports overriding the generated action, selecting a non-default root Lua script, and passing custom Premake command-line options through the public wrapper API. The update also refines the automatic MSVC-to-Premake action mapping so newer MSVC versions continue targeting the supported Visual Studio 2022 action.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the Premake CLI wrapper allows recipes to customize the Premake action, the root Lua script path, and additional command-line arguments while preserving automatic default action selection from compiler settings.

expectation.grounded: The public `conan.tools.premake.Premake` wrapper should expose configurable `action`, `luafile`, and `arguments` members. On construction, `action` should default from compiler settings to `vs2015`, `vs2017`, `vs2019`, or `vs2022` for MSVC versions `190`, `191`, `192`, `193`, and `194` respectively, and to `gmake2` for non-MSVC compilers. `luafile` should default to `premake5.lua`. Calling `Premake.configure()` should invoke `premake5` using the current `luafile`, the current `action`, and any custom `arguments` serialized as command-line options.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should be able to use the Premake wrapper as a configurable CLI front end instead of a fixed helper. By default it should still choose a sensible Premake action from the active compiler, but consumers must be able to point it at another Premake Lua entry file, override the action when needed, and append extra Premake options through the wrapper API.

constraints.grounded: Default behavior must remain stable for existing consumers that do not set the new members: non-MSVC builds should continue using the GNU Make 2 action, MSVC builds should still auto-select a Visual Studio action, and `Premake.configure()` should continue executing the `premake5` CLI. The generated command must reflect user-supplied overrides without requiring API changes beyond the wrapper's public members.
constraints.conceptual: The new configurability must extend the existing Premake integration without breaking the default experience. Existing recipes that rely on automatic action selection should keep working, while advanced consumers gain control over which Premake script and options are used.

behavior: Instantiating `Premake` now initializes a public `action` value automatically from compiler settings instead of deriving it only inside `configure()`.
MSVC compiler versions `193` and `194` both resolve to the Premake Visual Studio 2022 action, while earlier supported MSVC versions keep their corresponding Visual Studio actions.
The wrapper now exposes a public `luafile` value, defaulting to `premake5.lua`, and `configure()` passes that file to the `premake5` invocation.
The wrapper now exposes a public `arguments` dictionary, and each key/value entry is emitted as an additional `--key=value` option when `configure()` runs.
If a consumer changes `action`, `luafile`, or `arguments` before calling `configure()`, the generated `premake5` command uses those updated values.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe creates `Premake` without overriding any fields, it should still run `premake5` with an automatically selected action based on the active compiler and use `premake5.lua` as the script file.
When the active compiler is MSVC version `194`, calling `Premake.configure()` should target the Premake Visual Studio 2022 action rather than introducing a separate newer Visual Studio action.
When a recipe sets `Premake.luafile` to a custom Lua file before `configure()`, the resulting `premake5` invocation should use that file as the Premake entry point.
When a recipe sets `Premake.arguments` with one or more option pairs before `configure()`, the resulting `premake5` invocation should include each option as a corresponding command-line argument.
When a recipe overrides `Premake.action` before `configure()`, the wrapper should honor that explicit action instead of forcing the auto-detected default.

task_14.title: Add experimental `conan lock upgrade` command
task_14.description: Conan 2.13.0 introduces an experimental `lock upgrade` command that refreshes selected dependencies in an existing lockfile by resolving the dependency graph again. This removes the need to manually delete lock entries first or to preselect the exact replacement version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan provides an experimental `lock upgrade` workflow that can refresh one or more selected dependencies in an existing lockfile by resolving the graph again, without requiring users to manually remove lock entries or choose the exact replacement version in advance.

expectation.grounded: Expose a `conan lock upgrade` subcommand that accepts common graph inputs, works from either a conanfile path or reference-based graph arguments, and lets users select upgrade targets with `--update-requires`, `--update-build-requires`, `--update-python-requires`, and `--update-config-requires`. The command should require at least one of those selectors and raise `ConanException` otherwise. For the selected references, it should refresh the corresponding lockfile entries by resolving the graph with the active profiles, remotes, lockfile overrides, and `--update` settings, then save the resulting lockfile to `--lockfile-out` or to `conan.lock` by default. It should also support treating the resolved input as a build requirement when `--build-require` is provided.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to upgrade specific locked dependencies directly from the CLI. Conan should determine the new concrete versions through normal dependency resolution using the current project graph and configuration, then write back an updated lockfile.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade flow must preserve the distinction between regular requires, build-requires, python-requires, and config-requires based on the corresponding `--update-*` options. It must continue to honor standard graph-resolution controls supplied to the command, and it must not require callers to remove lock entries first or pin an explicit target version before upgrading.
constraints.conceptual: Only the dependency groups explicitly requested for upgrade should be refreshed, and the command should behave like a normal graph resolution operation rather than a manual lockfile editing step.

behavior: Adds an experimental `conan lock upgrade` subcommand for upgrading selected references from an existing lockfile.
Supports selecting upgrade targets independently for regular, build, python, and config requirements through dedicated `--update-*` options, with multiple selections allowed.
Rejects invocations that do not specify any `--update-*` selector by raising a `ConanException`.
Resolves the dependency graph again from either a conanfile path or reference-based graph input while using the current profiles, remotes, lockfile overrides, and update settings.

Refreshes the selected lockfile entries to the versions and revisions chosen by graph resolution and writes the updated lockfile to the requested output path or to `conan.lock` when no output path is supplied.
Supports build-require resolution mode for the provided input when `--build-require` is used.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing lockfile and a newer compatible regular requirement, when `conan lock upgrade` is run with `--update-requires` for that reference, then the resulting lockfile should contain the newly resolved locked reference instead of the previous one.

Given build, python, or config requirements in a lockfile, when the matching `--update-build-requires`, `--update-python-requires`, or `--update-config-requires` options are used, then Conan should refresh those dependency categories through normal graph resolution.

When `conan lock upgrade` is invoked without any `--update-requires`, `--update-build-requires`, `--update-python-requires`, or `--update-config-requires` option, it should fail with a `ConanException` instead of proceeding.
Given either a conanfile path or reference-based graph input, when the command resolves the upgrade, then it should use the active profile, remote, override, and update settings for graph resolution.

When a selected dependency is upgraded, users should not need to remove the prior lock entry or specify the exact target version beforehand; Conan should choose the concrete replacement during graph resolution.
When the command succeeds without `--lockfile-out`, it should write the updated lockfile to `conan.lock`, and when `--lockfile-out` is provided, it should write to that destination.

task_13.title: Allow Conan 2.13.0 to resolve with urllib3 2.0.x
task_13.description: Conan 2.13.0 broadens its urllib3 dependency range so compatible environments can use urllib3 2.0.x instead of being restricted to the 1.26 line, reducing installation conflicts while preserving compatibility with older supported urllib3 releases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.13.0 removes the previous restriction that blocked compatible urllib3 2.0 releases, while still allowing environments that need the older urllib3 1.26 series to install and use Conan successfully.

expectation.grounded: Conan 2.13.0 should declare urllib3 compatibility in the public version range >=1.26.6 and <2.1 rather than limiting urllib3 to <1.27. Dependency resolution for Conan should therefore accept urllib3 2.0.x on supported Python environments, while still permitting resolution to compatible urllib3 1.26.x versions when newer urllib3 releases are not applicable.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should expand Conan's supported urllib3 versions so users can install it alongside urllib3 2.x where that ecosystem is supported, without breaking users who still depend on the 1.26.x line.

constraints.grounded: Do not make urllib3 2.x mandatory. Conan must remain installable with urllib3 1.26.6+ releases, and the accepted urllib3 range must stop before 2.1. The change should preserve compatibility expectations for environments that do not receive urllib3 2.x.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a compatibility expansion, not a forced migration. Older valid environments must keep working, and unsupported newer urllib3 versions must remain outside the allowed range.

behavior: Conan's dependency resolution now permits urllib3 2.0.x instead of rejecting all urllib3 versions >=1.27.
Conan remains compatible with urllib3 1.26.6 and newer releases within the 1.26 series.
Dependency resolution should continue to reject urllib3 2.1 and newer releases.
Environments that cannot use urllib3 2.x should still be able to resolve Conan against a compatible urllib3 1.26.x release.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs Conan 2.13.0 in an environment where urllib3 2.0.x is otherwise valid, the dependency resolver should be able to select urllib3 2.0.x without a Conan-imposed version conflict.
When a user installs Conan 2.13.0 in an environment using urllib3 1.26.6 or newer within the 1.26 series, the installation should remain valid.
When dependency resolution encounters urllib3 2.1 or newer, Conan 2.13.0 should not advertise compatibility with those versions.
When a Python environment does not receive urllib3 2.x, upgrading to Conan 2.13.0 should still allow resolution to a compatible older urllib3 release instead of requiring urllib3 2.x.

task_16.title: Clarify `conan remote auth` username environment variable guidance
task_16.description: Conan 2.13.0 corrects the user-facing help for `conan remote auth` so automation and CI users are directed to the proper username environment variable family, `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*`, instead of the older `CONAN_LOGIN*` wording. The update also aligns the `--with-user` option help with that naming so credential discovery expectations are clearer.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan remote auth` user guidance names the correct username environment variables for non-interactive remote authentication, so users relying on CLI help for CI, scripting, or `--with-user` filtering are directed to `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` rather than ambiguous `CONAN_LOGIN*` references.

expectation.grounded: The public help text for `conan remote auth` should describe username-based authentication input as coming from `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` variables together with `CONAN_PASSWORD*` variables. The `--with-user` option help should state that it applies to remotes that already have a username or a matching `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` environment variable defined.
expectation.conceptual: Users reading the CLI help for remote authentication should see the correct environment variable names for providing usernames in automated workflows, and option help should consistently explain when a remote is considered to already have user credentials.

constraints.grounded: This update should not change the command's authentication flow, password variable family, prompting behavior, or remote selection rules beyond correcting the documented username variable name exposed in help and command descriptions.
constraints.conceptual: The change is limited to clarifying user-facing guidance. Existing authentication behavior and command semantics should remain the same.

behavior: The `conan remote auth` command description refers to `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` as the username environment variable family used for authentication guidance.
The `--with-user` option help refers to `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` when describing remotes that qualify as already having user credentials available.
The command continues to present `CONAN_PASSWORD*` as the password environment variable family alongside the corrected username variable naming.
The upgrade affects visible CLI documentation and help text rather than runtime authentication logic.
acceptance_criteria: When a user inspects the help or command description for `conan remote auth`, it should identify `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` as the username environment variable pattern used for authentication guidance.
When a user inspects the help for `conan remote auth --with-user`, it should describe the option in terms of remotes with an existing username or a `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME*` variable.

When users rely on the CLI help to configure scripted authentication, the documented username variable naming should be consistent with the intended public contract and should not suggest `CONAN_LOGIN*` as the username variable family.
The update should not introduce any new authentication requirements or alter how the command behaves at runtime.

task_18.title: Clarify CMakeDeps tool-require linking guidance
task_18.description: The incubating CMakeDeps guidance shown to users during integration now distinguishes tool requirements from linkable package requirements. Tool-requires remain discoverable through find_package guidance, but they are explicitly treated as non-linkable so consumers are not told to add them to target_link_libraries.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that incubating CMakeDeps does not instruct consumers to link targets coming from tool requirements, while still showing the relevant package discovery guidance for those dependencies.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeDeps emits its integration help for direct dependencies, direct tool-requires in the build context should still appear as find_package(...) entries, but they should be marked as optional and excluded from the suggested target_link_libraries(...) line. Only direct non-build requirements with linkable targets should contribute to the target_link_libraries(...) guidance.
expectation.conceptual: Users should see accurate CMake integration instructions: packages needed only as tools may still need discovery, but they must not be presented as libraries that should be linked into consumer targets.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove find_package(...) guidance for direct tool-requires. Do not include tool-requires in target_link_libraries(...) suggestions. Preserve existing link guidance for normal direct package requirements and continue omitting link suggestions for dependencies that do not expose linkable library targets.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should narrow misleading guidance without hiding legitimate dependency discovery steps or changing how normal library dependencies are presented.

behavior: CMakeDeps tracks whether each direct dependency is a normal requirement or a build-context tool-require when composing user-facing CMake guidance.
The printed find_package(...) guidance includes a note for tool-requires indicating that the dependency is optional in that context and that its targets are not meant to be linked.
The printed target_link_libraries(...) guidance is assembled only from direct, non-build dependencies that expose linkable targets.
If the direct dependencies only contribute tool-requires or other non-linkable entries, CMakeDeps should avoid printing a target_link_libraries(...) suggestion for those entries.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer installs dependencies with incubating CMakeDeps and a direct dependency is declared as a tool-require, the help output should still include a find_package(...) entry for that package.
When that dependency is a tool-require, the help output should identify it as non-linkable rather than implying it belongs in target_link_libraries(...).
When direct host requirements expose normal CMake targets, the help output should continue to include those targets in target_link_libraries(...).
When no direct dependency provides a linkable library target, the help output should not suggest linking tool-require targets.

task_17.title: Preserve Shared-Library Symlinks in runtime_deploy
task_17.description: Conan 2.13.0 fixes the runtime deployer so shared-library deployment includes versioned library filenames and preserves symbolic-link aliases when symlink deployment is enabled. This prevents deployed applications from missing the runtime library names they expect to load.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `runtime_deploy` deploys shared libraries with the runtime-visible names applications expect, instead of only copying the resolved library file and omitting versioned shared-library entries or symlink aliases.

expectation.grounded: When `conan install` uses the `runtime_deploy` deployer, shared libraries matched by `*.so*` and `*.dylib*` should be eligible for deployment. If `tools.deployer:symlinks` is enabled, symbolic-link files among those runtime libraries should be copied as symbolic links so aliases such as soname links remain available in the deploy folder. If `tools.deployer:symlinks` is disabled, symbolic-link entries should be skipped and only the concrete library files should be copied.
expectation.conceptual: Runtime deployment should include the actual shared library plus the alias names the dynamic loader expects when symlink handling is enabled, so deployed applications can resolve libraries normally. When symlink handling is disabled, deployment should still provide the real library file without emitting the link aliases.

constraints.grounded: The change should stay limited to `runtime_deploy` shared-library selection and copy behavior. Deployment remains flattened into the target folder, existing duplicate-content skipping behavior should continue, and missing library directories should still be reported without adding subfolder-preservation behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve runtime compatibility without changing the deployer's overall layout model or turning it into a different deployment mode.

behavior: `runtime_deploy` now treats versioned shared-library filenames as deployable runtime artifacts instead of only exact `.so` or `.dylib` suffixes.
With symlink deployment enabled, library symlink entries are preserved as symlinks in the output instead of being collapsed into only the resolved target file.
With symlink deployment disabled, symlink entries are not emitted into the deploy folder and only non-link runtime library files are copied.
Applications that rely on runtime loader aliases such as `.so` or soname symlinks can find those names in the deployed runtime folder when symlink deployment is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: When a package contains a versioned shared-library chain such as a real binary plus `.so` symlink aliases, running `conan install` with `--deployer=runtime_deploy` and symlink deployment enabled should place both the real library file and its symlink aliases in the deploy folder.
When the same package is deployed with symlink deployment disabled, the deploy folder should contain the real shared library file but not the symlink alias entries.

When a dependency exposes runtime libraries through versioned `.so*` or `.dylib*` filenames, `runtime_deploy` should include them as deployable runtime artifacts instead of ignoring them because they do not end in the bare extension.
When the deploy folder already contains an identical runtime artifact, the deployer should continue to avoid redundant replacement.

task_20.title: Propagate build-profile conf into GNU cross-build toolchains
task_20.description: Conan 2.13.0 fixes GNU toolchain generation for cross-building consumers so build-profile configuration is available through `conf_build` and can drive build-context compiler executable selection. This ensures build-machine compiler settings from `tools.build:compiler_executables` are honored when generating Autotools and GNU toolchains instead of being unavailable or ignored.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that cross-building consumers using `AutotoolsToolchain` or `GnuToolchain` can read build-context configuration from the build profile `conf`, so build-machine compiler executables are correctly applied during toolchain generation.

expectation.grounded: When a consumer is defined with separate host and build profiles, the consumer conanfile should expose build-profile configuration through `conf_build`. During cross-building, `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain` should read `tools.build:compiler_executables` from `conf_build` and use that build-context mapping when generating the toolchain environment for build-machine compilers.
expectation.conceptual: Cross-build toolchains should honor compiler executable settings from the build profile, not just the host profile, so generated GNU-based toolchains use the correct compilers for build-machine tasks.

constraints.grounded: This behavior should apply to consumer toolchain generation in cross-building scenarios only, preserve the existing use of host-profile `conf` for host-context settings, and avoid regressing `AutotoolsToolchain` or `GnuToolchain` behavior when build-profile compiler executable configuration is absent.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only affect build-context resolution for cross-builds, keep current target-context behavior intact, and remain safe when no build-profile compiler override is provided.

behavior: Consumer conanfiles now receive a `conf_build` view derived from the build profile configuration.
When cross-building with `AutotoolsToolchain`, build-context compiler executable settings from `tools.build:compiler_executables` are taken from the build profile configuration.
When cross-building with `GnuToolchain`, build-context compiler executable settings from `tools.build:compiler_executables` are taken from the build profile configuration.

Build-context compiler selection for GNU toolchains becomes observable through generated toolchain environment values for build-machine compiler variables, rather than depending on host-profile configuration.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer install uses separate host and build profiles and cross-building is active, `AutotoolsToolchain` should honor `tools.build:compiler_executables` from the build profile for build-context compiler selection.

When a consumer install uses separate host and build profiles and cross-building is active, `GnuToolchain` should honor `tools.build:compiler_executables` from the build profile for build-context compiler selection.

When host and build profiles define different compiler executable mappings, the generated build-context compiler configuration should follow the build profile mapping rather than the host profile mapping.
When no build-profile compiler executable mapping is provided, GNU toolchain generation should continue without introducing new failures solely because `conf_build` is consulted.

task_21.title: Support custom separators in profile environment variables
task_21.description: The upgrade adds support for declaring explicit separators for profile-defined environment variables so inherited values, especially Windows-style semicolon-separated variables used through the msys2 subsystem, are composed correctly. It also preserves that separator metadata in serialized environment output and rejects invalid combinations with path-style qualifiers.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that profile-defined environment variables can explicitly declare a non-default separator so inherited environment values remain correctly composed in subsystem builds such as msys2. Ensure that invalid profile entries combining custom-separator semantics with path-style semantics are rejected.

expectation.grounded: Conan profile environment entries must accept a `(sep=<char>)` qualifier for variable definitions and `+=` / `=+` updates, and use that separator when composing the resulting environment value with existing inherited values. Environment serialization must preserve `(sep=<char>)` for non-default separators, and parsing a profile entry that combines `(sep=<char>)` with `(path)` must raise `ConanException` instead of producing an environment value.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare how a profile-managed environment variable is joined when it inherits or combines with existing values, so Windows-style lists such as semicolon-separated include or path variables work correctly in subsystem-based builds. Conan should keep that declared separator visible when it reports the environment configuration, and it should fail fast on ambiguous qualifier combinations.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the behavior of environment entries that do not declare `(sep=<char>)`. Treat custom-separator entries as regular environment variables rather than `(path)` variables, and reject any entry that tries to apply both qualifier types simultaneously. Preserve the declared custom separator in dumped profile environment output.
constraints.conceptual: Existing profiles without an explicit custom separator should continue to behave as before. Custom joining rules must not silently trigger path-specific rewriting, and ambiguous profile syntax should be rejected instead of guessed.

behavior: Profile environment entries can define an explicit separator with `(sep=<char>)` before the value content.
The custom separator applies to direct definitions as well as appended and prepended profile environment entries.
When the final environment value is composed with inherited or already-defined values, Conan joins the segments using the declared separator instead of the default delimiter.
Serialized or displayed profile environment output retains the `(sep=<char>)` qualifier for non-default separators so the configuration round-trips accurately.
If a profile entry combines `(sep=<char>)` and `(path)`, Conan rejects it by raising `ConanException`.
acceptance_criteria: When a profile defines an environment variable with `(sep=@)` and that variable later receives another value, the resulting environment value should join the segments with `@`.

When a profile prepends and appends to an inherited semicolon-separated variable using `(sep=;)`, the resulting environment variable should preserve the inherited values and join all profile and inherited segments with `;`.
When Conan serializes a profile environment entry that uses a custom separator, the serialized form should still indicate `(sep=<char>)`.
When a profile entry combines a custom separator qualifier with a path qualifier, Conan should fail with `ConanException`.
When a profile environment entry omits `(sep=<char>)`, its behavior should remain unchanged from previous releases.

task_19.title: Fix CycloneDX SBOM license calculation
task_19.description: Conan 2.13.0 fixes a CycloneDX SBOM generation bug so each component's license metadata is taken from that component itself. This corrects inaccurate SBOM output for recipes that declare multiple licenses and prevents license data from being attributed from another component in the graph.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CycloneDX SBOM generation reports each component's declared licenses correctly, including recipes that declare multiple licenses, without borrowing license entries from another component in the dependency graph.

expectation.grounded: In `conan.tools.sbom.cyclonedx.cyclonedx_1_4`, the `licenses` field for each emitted component must be derived from that same component's `conanfile.license` value. If `license` is a string, the component should expose one CycloneDX license entry. If `license` is a sequence such as a list or tuple, the component should expose one license entry per declared identifier from that component, and the result must not depend on any previously iterated component.
expectation.conceptual: Generating a CycloneDX SBOM should preserve every package's own declared license information at the component level. Packages with one license should show one license entry, and packages with multiple declared licenses should show all of them under the correct component regardless of what else is present in the graph.

constraints.grounded: Keep the existing CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM structure and non-license behavior unchanged: components that have no declared license should continue omitting the `licenses` field, and existing component inclusion, dependency references, and other metadata should not change as part of this fix.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to correcting license reporting accuracy and should not alter which components appear in the SBOM or how unrelated SBOM fields behave.

behavior: `cyclonedx_1_4` calculates a component's `licenses` entries from that component's own `conanfile.license` value when building the CycloneDX SBOM.
Recipes that declare multiple licenses as a list or tuple produce one license entry per declared license identifier in the generated component record.
License data no longer leaks from another component due to graph iteration order when multiple components are present in the SBOM.
Recipes that declare a single string license continue to produce a single license entry for that component.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares a single license string and a CycloneDX SBOM is generated, its component entry should contain exactly one matching license entry.
When a package declares multiple licenses as a list or tuple and a CycloneDX SBOM is generated, its component entry should contain one license entry for each declared license.

When multiple components are present in the SBOM, each component's `licenses` field should reflect only that component's declared licenses and should not change based on the position or license values of other components.
When a component has no declared license, CycloneDX SBOM generation should continue without adding unrelated license data to that component.

task_22.title: Clarify component and runtime conflict errors
task_22.description: Conan 2.13.0 improves diagnostic output for invalid component dependency declarations in package metadata and for runtime-only dependency graph conflicts, so package authors can understand why resolution failed and which packages or components are involved.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that invalid component dependency definitions and runtime-only package conflicts produce clear, actionable errors that identify the failing relationship and the affected packages or components.
