expectation.grounded: During `package_info()` validation of `cpp_info.requires` and `cpp_info.components[*].requires`, Conan should raise `ConanException` with issue-specific diagnostics for undefined internal component references, references to packages that are not direct requirements, and direct dependencies that are not referenced by any external component requirement. Runtime-only graph conflicts should continue to surface as `GraphRuntimeError`, but the reported error should explain that the conflict happens at runtime, point users toward package type and `run=True` trait review, and include both conflicting package references.
expectation.conceptual: Users should receive error messages that clearly distinguish misconfigured component requirements from runtime dependency conflicts. The errors should tell them what kind of mismatch occurred, which package or component caused it, and whether the conflict is specific to runtime composition rather than compile-time dependency resolution.

constraints.grounded: Keep the existing failure modes tied to the same public surfaces: component-definition issues remain `ConanException` failures during `package_info()` validation, and runtime graph clashes remain `GraphRuntimeError` failures during graph processing. Valid dependency declarations should continue to proceed without new warnings or altered success behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Improve diagnostics without changing the expected success path for correctly declared dependencies. Errors should be more informative, not broader in scope or triggered in unrelated scenarios.

behavior: If `cpp_info.requires` or `cpp_info.components[*].requires` refers to internal components that are not defined, Conan raises `ConanException` that identifies the missing internal component names as a `package_info()` component-definition problem.
If a component requirement references a package namespace that is not among the recipe's direct requirements, Conan raises `ConanException` that identifies the undeclared package reference.
If a direct dependency covered by component validation is not referenced by any external component requirement, Conan raises `ConanException` that identifies that unused direct dependency.

When a runtime-only dependency conflict is detected in the graph, `GraphRuntimeError` describes it as a runtime conflict, explains the runtime nature of the clash, and reports both conflicting package references.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe declares component requirements to internal components that do not exist, package creation should fail with a `ConanException` that identifies the missing internal components.
When a recipe declares a component requirement on a package that is not a direct dependency, package creation should fail with a `ConanException` that identifies that package reference as invalid.

When a direct dependency expected by component validation is not referenced by any external component requirement, package creation should fail with a `ConanException` that identifies the unused direct dependency.

When dependency graph resolution encounters a runtime-only conflict between two packages, the reported `GraphRuntimeError` should explain that the conflict is runtime-specific and include both package references in the report.

task_23.title: Correct Conan client migration success output for compatibility.py updates
task_23.description: The Conan 2.13.0 upgrade fixes the client migration success output shown when migrating compatibility settings so that the notification is properly formatted and clearly identifies the updated compatibility file.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan client migration output for compatibility file updates is correctly formatted and does not show malformed success text when upgrading.

expectation.grounded: When Conan runs client migration logic that updates `compatibility.py`, the CLI should emit a `ConanOutput.success` notification for that migration event with a properly formatted reference to `compatibility.py`. The success notification should only appear when the migration path actually updates an existing non-default compatibility file.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading Conan should see a clean, correctly formatted success notice if the migration updates their compatibility configuration, and they should not see malformed migration text.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the migration trigger conditions, the decision to rewrite `compatibility.py`, or the surrounding migration flow. Preserve the existing behavior that the success notification is tied to an actual compatibility file update and avoid introducing malformed characters into the emitted output.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the migration behavior unchanged apart from correcting the user-visible output. The fix should improve message quality without altering when migration runs or what files it updates.

behavior: A successful client migration that updates `compatibility.py` now produces a well-formed success notification instead of malformed output.
The success notification explicitly refers to the compatibility file update associated with migration.
The success notification remains conditional on the migration path that updates an existing non-default compatibility configuration.
acceptance_criteria: When upgrading Conan causes client migration to update an existing non-default `compatibility.py`, the CLI should show a success notification for that update.
When that success notification is shown, it should be correctly formatted and should not contain stray trailing characters.
When the migration does not update an existing non-default `compatibility.py`, Conan should not emit the compatibility update success notification.

task_26.title: Fix CMakeDeps transitive linking for shared libraries
task_26.description: Conan 2.13.0 fixes the new CMakeDeps generator so transitive shared-library dependencies are modeled correctly in generated CMake targets. Shared libraries now propagate compile usage and dependent shared-library information without forcing incorrect full-link behavior between shared libraries, while preserving normal transitive linking for other dependency types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the new `CMakeDeps` generator correctly handles transitive dependencies when a shared library or shared component depends on another shared library, so downstream consumers receive the needed dependency information without incorrect full-link propagation.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeDeps` generates package or component targets, it should distinguish normal link requirements from shared-to-shared transitive requirements. If a shared package or shared component requires another shared package or shared component, the generated imported target should expose that dependency for compile usage and record it as a dependent shared library instead of treating it as a normal full `INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES` link. For package-level targets, same-package component requirements, cross-package component requirements, and aggregate interface targets, non-shared dependency relationships should continue to propagate as normal link requirements. If this shared-to-shared handling is needed with CMake lower than 3.27, configuration should fail with a fatal error.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading should make transitive shared-library usage work correctly with `CMakeDeps`: shared libraries should no longer over-link other shared libraries, but downstream consumers should still inherit the required dependency information and build successfully. Existing non-shared transitive linking behavior should remain intact, and unsupported CMake versions should fail clearly instead of producing incorrect linkage.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress standard transitive linking for static or otherwise non-shared dependency relationships. Do not break package-level aggregate targets, default-component aggregate targets, or component-based requirements within the same package or across packages. Aggregate interface targets should continue to fully link to their member targets where full linkage is intended.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the fix limited to the incorrect shared-to-shared propagation case. Existing dependency consumption patterns, especially component-based and aggregate target consumption, should continue to behave as before unless the old behavior was specifically wrong for shared-library transitives.

behavior: `CMakeDeps` now classifies each transitive requirement as either a normal full link requirement or a shared-to-shared dependent-library relationship.

When a shared package or shared component depends on another shared package or shared component, the generated target exposes that requirement for compile usage and separately records the dependent shared library instead of adding it as a normal full interface link.
When the dependency relationship is not shared-to-shared, generated targets continue to propagate the dependency through normal interface link requirements.
Package-level and default-component aggregate interface targets continue to fully link to their member targets.
If a generated target needs the shared-to-shared handling and the consumer uses CMake earlier than 3.27, configuration fails with a fatal compatibility error.
acceptance_criteria: When a package generated with `CMakeDeps` exposes a shared library that transitively depends on another shared library, downstream consumers should still receive the dependency information needed to configure and link correctly without manual transitive-link workarounds.

When a shared library target depends on another shared library target through package or component requirements, the generated CMake target should not treat that dependency as a normal full interface link between shared libraries.
When the dependency is static or otherwise not a shared-to-shared relationship, `CMakeDeps` should preserve normal transitive link propagation behavior.
When packages use components or default components, consumers should still be able to link through the generated package/component targets and receive the expected dependency propagation.
When the shared-to-shared transitive fix is required under CMake 3.26 or earlier, configuration should stop with a fatal error instead of producing an incorrect target model.

task_24.title: Improve tar.gz extraction performance and strip-root validation
task_24.description: Updates tar.gz extraction to avoid re-reading archives during selective unpacking, improving runtime and preventing progress reporting from exceeding 100%. The upgrade also makes root-stripping behavior stricter and more predictable by only allowing it for archives whose extracted entries share a single top-level directory and by preserving correct extraction of links under that stripped root.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that tar.gz extraction stays efficient and reports realistic progress when unpacking archives, including filtered extractions and root-folder stripping. Ensure that root-folder stripping only succeeds when the relevant archive entries belong to one shared top-level directory, and fails for archives that place files directly in the archive root or mix different top-level roots.

expectation.grounded: For `conan.tools.files.untargz()`, extracting `.tar.gz` archives with `pattern` and/or `strip_root=True` should process matching members in a single extraction pass instead of preloading the full archive, so large archives unpack faster and untar progress does not overshoot completion. When `strip_root=True`, the extracted member names should be rewritten relative to one common top-level directory discovered from the relevant entries, and link targets under that same root should also be rewritten consistently. If the relevant archive entries contain files directly at the archive root, or entries from more than one top-level root, the operation should fail with `ConanException` rather than partially extracting inconsistent output.
expectation.conceptual: Selective tar.gz extraction should be faster and should not appear to run past 100% progress. When `strip_root` is enabled, extraction should remove exactly one shared top-level directory from the extracted content, preserve valid links under that directory, and reject archives that do not have a single removable root.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the normal full-archive path when neither `pattern` nor `strip_root` is used. Continue honoring archive extraction filtering, pattern-based inclusion, and link extraction behavior, while preventing partial success for invalid `strip_root` layouts.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve existing extraction behavior for ordinary tar.gz unpacking, keep filtering behavior intact, and add stricter validation only for root-stripping scenarios that would otherwise produce ambiguous or incorrect output.

behavior: `untargz()` should unpack matching `.tar.gz` entries in a single pass when `pattern` or `strip_root` is used, improving runtime and avoiding progress values above completion.
When `strip_root=True`, the extraction root should be derived from the first relevant archive member and removed from extracted paths.
When `strip_root=True`, archives whose relevant entries include files directly in the archive root should raise `ConanException`.
When `strip_root=True`, archives whose relevant entries span more than one top-level root should raise `ConanException`.
When stripping the common root from link entries, link targets that point within that root should also be rewritten so extracted links remain valid.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller extracts a large `.tar.gz` archive with `pattern` filtering or `strip_root=True`, the extraction should complete without a second full archive scan and should not report untar progress above 100%.

When a caller extracts a `.tar.gz` archive with `strip_root=True` and all relevant entries share one top-level directory, the extracted output should omit that directory and place the contained files directly under the destination.
When a caller extracts a `.tar.gz` archive with `strip_root=True` and the relevant entries include one or more files directly at the archive root, the extraction should fail with `ConanException`.
When a caller extracts a `.tar.gz` archive with `strip_root=True` and the relevant entries come from multiple top-level roots, the extraction should fail with `ConanException`.
When a caller extracts a `.tar.gz` archive with `strip_root=True` that contains links under the stripped root, the extracted links should continue to reference the correct relative targets.

task_25.title: Protect read-only CppInfo.required_components access
task_25.description: The upgrade hardens the CppInfo API so accidental assignment to the computed required_components property is rejected immediately instead of being accepted through attribute forwarding. This prevents invalid recipe state and preserves required component resolution as a read-only derived view.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that accidental writes to CppInfo.required_components are rejected as invalid, so users can inspect required component relationships without being able to overwrite the computed result.

expectation.grounded: CppInfo.required_components must remain a read-only computed property in Conan 2.13.0. Reading it should continue to expose the aggregated required-component view derived from declared package and component .requires entries. Assigning to cpp_info.required_components must fail immediately with AttributeError instead of being redirected to the underlying package component state.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to read the resolved required component information, but they must not be able to assign to that property directly. Invalid writes should surface as a clear API error, while normal requirement aggregation continues to behave the same.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing computed semantics of required_components, including aggregation from declared .requires entries and preservation of internal versus external requirement interpretation. Valid assignments to other CppInfo fields must continue to work through the existing API behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to protecting the read-only property. It must not change how valid CppInfo configuration works or alter the dependency information returned when the property is read.

behavior: Assigning any value to cpp_info.required_components raises AttributeError.
The write is no longer silently accepted or forwarded into package-backed CppInfo state.
Reading CppInfo.required_components still returns the aggregated required-component view derived from declared package-level and component-level .requires entries.
The computed view continues to distinguish internal component requirements from external package-qualified requirements.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe reads cpp_info.required_components after declaring valid .requires entries, it should receive the computed aggregated required-component information.
When a recipe attempts to assign a value to cpp_info.required_components, it should fail immediately with AttributeError.
When valid writable CppInfo attributes are assigned, they should continue to behave as before.
When package-level and component-level requirements are both present, reading required_components should continue to reflect their combined resolved view.

task_27.title: Bundle new Conan tool namespaces in PyInstaller builds
task_27.description: The self-contained Conan executable built with PyInstaller must include newly added public tool namespaces so packaged Conan distributions can load those tools at runtime. This closes a packaging gap introduced by newer tool modules, most notably SBOM support.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the self-contained Conan executable generated with PyInstaller includes newly added `conan.tools` modules, especially `conan.tools.sbom`, so users can run packaged Conan workflows that depend on those tool namespaces without module-loading failures.

expectation.grounded: When Conan is distributed as a self-contained PyInstaller executable, the packaged application must include the public tool namespaces referenced by the updated hidden-import set, including `conan.tools.sbom` and the additional `conan.tools.android`, `conan.tools.ros`, and `conan.tools.scons` modules, while preserving availability of the existing `conan.tools.*` packages already bundled. Imports of these public tool modules from recipes, hooks, or CLI-driven workflows must resolve successfully in the packaged executable.
expectation.conceptual: The standalone Conan binary should behave like a normal installation for supported tool modules. After upgrading, workflows that rely on newly introduced Conan tool areas, especially SBOM generation, should work from the packaged executable without failing because those modules were omitted from the bundle.

constraints.grounded: This requirement applies to the PyInstaller-built self-contained executable path and must not remove support for previously bundled `conan.tools` namespaces. The change should affect module availability in packaged distributions only and should not alter the public behavior of regular Python-based installations.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand packaged-module coverage without regressing existing packaged workflows or changing behavior outside the standalone executable distribution.

behavior: PyInstaller-built Conan distributions now bundle the `conan.tools.sbom` namespace.
The packaged executable also includes additional public tool namespaces that were absent from the prior hidden-import list, including Android, ROS, and SCons tool modules.
Recipes, hooks, or commands executed through the self-contained Conan binary can import these bundled `conan.tools.*` modules without runtime module-missing failures caused by packaging omissions.
Previously bundled `conan.tools.*` namespaces remain available in the packaged executable.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan 2.13.0 is packaged as a self-contained PyInstaller executable and a workflow imports `conan.tools.sbom`, the import should succeed in the packaged runtime.
When the packaged executable runs a workflow that imports `conan.tools.android`, `conan.tools.ros`, or `conan.tools.scons`, it should not fail because those namespaces are missing from the bundle.
When existing packaged workflows import previously supported `conan.tools.*` namespaces, they should continue to work after the upgrade.
When Conan is used outside the PyInstaller self-contained distribution, this packaging fix should not change user-visible behavior.
